title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
description:
There are `n` people standing in a queue, numbered from `0` to `n - 1` from left to right. You are given an integer array `heights` of **distinct** positive integers where `heights[i]` represents the height of the `i`-th person.

Person `i` can **see** another person `j` to their right (`i < j`) if and only if everyone standing between them is shorter than both of them. Formally, person `i` can see person `j` when `i < j` and `min(heights[i], heights[j]) > max(heights[i + 1], heights[i + 2], ..., heights[j - 1])` (vacuously true when `j == i + 1`).

Return an array `answer` of length `n` where `answer[i]` is the number of people person `i` can see to their right in the queue.
constraints: All values of heights are unique.
hints: Process the queue from right to left while maintaining a monotonic decreasing stack of heights currently visible from the left.
For person `i`, pop every person from the stack shorter than `heights[i]`: person `i` can see each of them, and nobody to the left of `i` will be able to see past `i` to those shorter people.
After popping shorter people, if the stack is still non-empty, person `i` can also see the first taller person on top of the stack (add `1` to the count), then push `heights[i]`.

examples.explanation: Person 0 (10) sees 6, 8, and 11 (count 3). Person 1 (6) sees 8. Person 2 (8) sees 5 and 11. Person 5 (9) sees no one to their right.
Person 0 (5) sees all four people to their right (1, 2, 3, 10) because each is taller than everyone before them in the gap.
Every person except the last immediately hits a taller neighbor and sees exactly 1 person.
